name: North Carolina
uniformActsAdopted: Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act

citations.title: Power of attorney; durability
citations.quote: A power of attorney created pursuant to this Chapter is durable unless the instrument expressly provides that it is terminated by the incapacity of the principal.

citations.title: Termination of power of attorney
citations.quote: A power of attorney terminates when any of the following occur: (1) The principal dies. (2) If the power of attorney is not durable, the principal becomes incapacitated.

citations.title: Effectiveness and duration; revocation
citations.quote: A health care power of attorney shall become effective when and if the physician or physicians ... determine in writing that the principal lacks sufficient understanding or capacity

citations.title: Jurisdiction; authority of clerk
citations.quote: Clerks of superior court in their respective counties have original jurisdiction for the appointment of guardians of the person, guardians of the estate, or general guardians for incompetent persons

citations.title: Application for letters; grant of letters
citations.quote: The application for letters of administration or letters testamentary shall be in the form of an affidavit sworn to before an officer authorized to administer oaths

citations.title: Collection of property by affidavit when decedent dies intestate
citations.quote: When a decedent dies intestate leaving personal property, less liens and encumbrances thereon, not exceeding twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) in value, at any time after 30 days from the date of death

citations.title: User direction for disclosure of digital assets
citations.quote: a direction regarding disclosure using an online tool overrides a contrary direction by the user in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other record

citations.title: Authority to dispose of body or body parts
citations.quote: An individual at least 18 years of age may authorize the type, place, and method of disposition of the individual's own dead body

assigned.event: Principal executes a power of attorney under Chapter 32C

ends.event: Principal dies; revokes; the instrument's terms; purpose accomplished; or no agent remains

patches.diff: Durability is the default under Chapter 32C and must be opted out of expressly.

localNames: power of attorney expressly terminated by incapacity

ends.event: Principal becomes incapacitated, where the instrument expressly says so

patches.diff: Exists only where the principal opted out of durability in the instrument.

localNames: attorney-in-fact under a health care power of attorney

starts.event: Physicians designated by the principal determine in writing that the principal lacks sufficient understanding or capacity to make or communicate health care decisions

patches.diff: The determination must be in writing, and for mental health treatment it may be made by an eligible psychologist rather than a physician.

assigned.event: Clerk of superior court appoints; the clerk, not a judge, has original jurisdiction

patches.diff: Guardianship is a clerk of superior court matter in North Carolina, with original jurisdiction in the clerk rather than a judge.

assigned.event: Clerk of superior court appoints a guardian of the estate or a general guardian

patches.diff: North Carolina has no conservator: the property fiduciary is a guardian of the estate, or a general guardian covering both person and estate, appointed by the clerk.

starts.event: Clerk of superior court grants letters testamentary on a sworn application

patches.diff: The application for letters is itself a sworn affidavit, recorded and filed by the clerk of superior court.

starts.event: Clerk of superior court grants letters of administration on a sworn application

patches.diff: Same sworn-affidavit application and the same clerk of superior court as for letters testamentary.

starts.event: 30 days after death, where intestate personal property net of liens does not exceed $20,000

patches.diff: Collection by affidavit is limited to intestate estates, capped at $20,000 of personal property net of liens, and cannot be used until 30 days after death.

assigned.event: User directs disclosure through the custodian's online tool

patches.diff: North Carolina enacted RUFADAA as Chapter 36F; an online-tool direction overrides a contrary direction in a will, trust or power of attorney.

patches.name: Person authorised to dispose of the body
patches.summary: An adult may direct the type, place and method of disposition of their own body, through a ranked list of instruments beginning with a preneed funeral contract and a health care power of attorney.

assigned.event: Individual aged 18 or over authorises disposition by one of the ranked methods

transitions.event: Authorisation by preneed funeral contract, cremation authorization form or health care power of attorney (§130A-420(a))

patches.diff: North Carolina ranks the instruments that control disposition of a body, and a health care power of attorney is one of them. The uniform/model baseline has no equivalent role.
